quotations.text:
Final Status: FAILED (blocked by OS access restriction)

The script itself ran unchanged and unmodified every time. It failed cleanly at the single point of installing the WH_KEYBOARD_LL hook — Windows refused with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (WinError 5). No hook was ever installed, so nothing needed cleanup (cleanupErrors: []).

The program initialized correctly (Python 3.12.10, 64-bit, DPI-awareness set) and reached the hook-install stage, where SetWindowsHookExW(WH_KEYBOARD_LL=13, ...) returned a null handle with GetLastError() == 5. This is a Windows UIPI / integrity-level / session policy rejection of a global low-level keyboard hook, not a defect in the script and not something the tool sandbox toggles.
